title: Fixed-allocation / BMI call-start clock-lattice generalization

sequencing.rationale: Generalize H10 beyond one 5h/6h pair before adopting a generic effective-cadence rule.

derivation: For fixed allocation.dt in the inspected v2026.1.1 BMI path, update_allocation! is evaluated at BMI step start only.
With a regular 6 h BMI call-start grid, an allocation solve can therefore occur only at times belonging to both grids.
For integer-hour cadences, the repeating intersection interval is lcm(allocation_dt, 6 h).
The expected record grids are frozen from that intersection rule before H11 execution.
hypotheses: Observed allocation record times equal the preregistered intersections for all four cases.
A4 aliases to a 12 h effective solve interval, A5 to 30 h, A8 to 24 h, and aligned A6 remains 6 h.
No allocation record is created merely because a BMI update interval crosses a nominal fixed-allocation boundary.
Together with actual-product H10, this supports a clock-lattice contract for the tested fixed-dt v2026.1.1 BMI route.
forbidden: no post-output changes to expected grids
no claim for adaptive allocation mode
no claim for later Ribasim versions
no production prescription or defect classification
